label: early step right after "c" (esp. "dc"/"cc") on m/o/x/n/3/r or <DEL>
explanation: Very sparse feature (0.018% of steps). It fires almost only early in the sequence (t=2-4 hold about 92% of mass, with t=3 peaking) and only in the original or delimiter phase. It almost never fires in the copy phase. The main cue is that the previous input was "c" (69% of activations, 25x lift). Activations are strongest when the bigram before is "dc" or "cc" and the current token is one of m/o/x/n/3/r or <DEL>. The top examples look like "w d c [m]", "w c c [o]" and "e c c [o]". Previous tokens 3, 1 or d are weaker secondary contexts. Whether it fires also depends on the earlier context, such as the first token: "n d c n" does not fire while "w d c n" does. So it looks like a fuzzy conjunction over the recent hidden state. prev_tok==c alone has 0.4% precision. The best conjunction reaches F1 about 0.40 on dev (precision 0.48, recall 0.34). It does not fire at t=0-1, on repeated tokens (95% of mass is on the first occurrence of a token), or on later copy steps.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: prev_tok=c (+4.71), prev2_tok=d (+4.40), prev2_tok=c (+4.28), orig0=g (+4.18), prev_tok=3 (+3.27), orig1=w (+3.21). Lower it: phase=2 (-4.35), prev3_tok=g (-3.84), prev2_tok=w (-2.72), orig0=3 (-2.57).
